provenance: Extracted from the five sources added to the Source list in landmark-strategy-v1.md (2026-06-20). NOT independently verified — every entry requires a verification pass before public copy is written.

landmarks.name: Mechanics and Traders Bank of Brooklyn
landmarks.summary: 1895 Renaissance/Romanesque Revival bank at the Franklin/Greenpoint Ave corner; later home to Polish community organizations, converted to co-op in 1984. Within the Greenpoint Historic District.
storyHooks: Grandest building on its block on the old Williamsburg-Astoria turnpike
Bank merged into Corn Exchange Bank (1902) -> eventually Chase
landmarks.verificationNotes: Source-derived; architect unknown in sources. Confirm Historic District inclusion against LPC designation report.

landmarks.name: Public Bath on Huron Street (Greenpoint Bathhouse)
landmarks.summary: 1904 Classical Revival public bath by architect Louis A. Voss; served ~1,000 bathers/day and was Brooklyn's last operating public bath before closing in 1960. Later used by a gilding/framing shop and artist studios.
storyHooks: Public bath movement / tenement-era sanitation reform (Dr. Simon Baruch)
~89 shower stalls and tubs, separate gender entrances
landmarks.verificationNotes: Source-derived (Brooklyn Relics blog). Confirm address, dates, and architect against a primary/LPC source.

landmarks.name: Astral Apartments
landmarks.summary: 1885-1886 model worker housing built by Charles Pratt for Astral Oil Works employees; brick and terracotta in Queen Anne style.
storyHooks: Industrial paternalism and early apartment reform
landmarks.verificationNotes: Already a v1 Tier 1 priority in landmark-strategy-v1.md.

landmarks.name: Eberhard Faber Pencil Factory Historic District
landmarks.summary: Oldest pencil factory in America; the firm moved from Manhattan to Greenpoint in 1872 and the complex operated until 1956. Iconic German Renaissance Revival / Art Deco factory architecture with star-and-diamond motif.
storyHooks: Giant pencil facade elements; star-and-diamond motif
landmarks.verificationNotes: Already a v1 Tier 1 priority. Note source discrepancy on dates (Greenpoint move 1872 vs. district building dates); reconcile against LPC report.

landmarks.name: Greenpoint Historic District
landmarks.address: Java, Franklin, Kent, Milton, Noble, Calyer, Leonard, Oak, Guernsey, Lorimer Sts and surrounds
landmarks.summary: Residential district developed from 1832 around the shipbuilding industry; homes built by and for shipyard workers. Designated 1982. Base historic layer for v1 (render as a translucent overlay, not a pin).
storyHooks: Protected district boundaries and streetscape continuity
landmarks.verificationNotes: Already a v1 Tier 1 priority. Use LPC boundary data for the overlay.

landmarks.name: Manhattan Avenue Sidewalk Clock
landmarks.summary: Cast-iron street clock from the 1860s, the last remaining sidewalk clock in Brooklyn; originally advertised Bomelstein Jewelers.
landmarks.verificationNotes: On the v1 shortlist. Confirm date (1860s vs. later individual-landmark designation).

landmarks.name: PS 34 (Oliver H. Perry Elementary School)
landmarks.summary: Oldest continuously operational primary school in Brooklyn, built 1867 in Romanesque style.
storyHooks: Oldest continuously operating primary school in Brooklyn

landmarks.name: Winthrop Park Shelter Pavilion (McGolrick Park)
landmarks.address: McGolrick Park, Monitor/Russell/Nassau/Driggs Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11222
landmarks.summary: 1910 park shelter pavilion in McGolrick Park (formerly Winthrop Park), with French-inspired radial landscaping. Tour endpoint includes the WWI monument to Greenpointers.
landmarks.verificationNotes: On the v1 shortlist. Distinguish the pavilion landmark from the Monitor Monument.

landmarks.name: 19th Police Precinct Station House and Stable
landmarks.summary: Romanesque Revival police complex built 1891-92; an example of late-19th-century Brooklyn precinct architecture.
landmarks.verificationNotes: New from source. Confirm address and designation status.

landmarks.name: McCarren Play Center
landmarks.summary: Largest of eleven WPA-funded public pool complexes, built 1936 under Robert Moses.
landmarks.verificationNotes: New from source. Sits at the Greenpoint/Williamsburg edge near McCarren Park; check spine fit.

landmarks.name: Russian Orthodox Cathedral of the Transfiguration of Our Lord
landmarks.summary: Byzantine-style church completed 1921, with distinctive onion domes.
landmarks.verificationNotes: New from source. Southern edge of the neighborhood; check spine fit.

landmarks.name: Greenpoint Savings Bank
landmarks.summary: 1906 neo-Classical bank at the southwest corner of Manhattan Ave and Calyer St, with a low dome and columned portico entrance.
storyHooks: "Where locals stored their money" tour theme
landmarks.verificationNotes: New from Clio. Confirm landmark/designation status and current tenant.

landmarks.name: Smithsonian Hall
landmarks.summary: Three-story cast-iron building (1878-early 1879) built to hold a ground-floor clothing store with a performance hall on the upper stories — the tour's namesake "Other Smithsonian."
landmarks.verificationNotes: New from Clio. Confirm address, dates, and current condition/use.

landmarks.name: Hecla Iron Works Building
landmarks.summary: 1896-97 headquarters and showroom for a Scandinavian-founded ironworks whose decorative metalwork appears across NYC.
landmarks.verificationNotes: New from source but located in WILLIAMSBURG, outside the v1 Greenpoint spine. Held pending scope decision.
